title: 第十七章 风声第十六章 银丝
lines: 陈志远的电话之后，沈南枝忙了整整一个礼拜。
银花系列的订单还没来，但她得先把材料备齐。0.3毫米的银丝在京海买不到，她托陈志远从滨海发了五十卷过来，运费比银丝本身还贵。紫水晶和粉晶的库存也不够，她又联系了广州的供货商，加急订了一批，对方说要等十天。
这十天不能闲着。她让县城的六个女工全部转去做基础款的串珠饰品，京海的十个人分成两组，一组做“京海之春”的常规补货，一组跟着她学银丝的编织手法。
教人的过程比她想的累得多。
十个人里，手最巧的是张嫂。别看她五大三粗的，手指头粗得像胡萝卜，但捏起银丝来稳得很，绕第一圈的时候手不抖，收尾的时候线头藏得干净。沈南枝教了三遍她就学会了，虽然速度慢，编一朵花要二十多分钟，但至少编出来的东西能看。
有两个年轻的姑娘手也巧，学得快，但没耐心，编了两朵就觉得行了，开始聊天说笑。沈南枝把她们编的花并排放在桌上，指着其中一朵花瓣歪了的说，“这个拿出去卖，三毛钱都没人要”。两个姑娘脸红了，低下头继续练。
剩下的七个，怎么教都教不会。不是手抖就是绕错方向，有的连钳子都拿不稳。沈南枝没勉强她们，让她们回去继续做串珠，计件工资照旧。
最后能上手编银花的，只有张嫂和那两个年轻姑娘。四个人，包括沈南枝自己，每天最多能编四五十朵银花，远远不够。
她需要更多人手，更好的人手。
这个问题在脑子里转了好几天，没找到解法。
这天傍晚，沈南枝在仓库里清点材料。银丝到了三十卷，还有二十卷在路上。紫水晶来了两箱，她拆开一箱，抓了一把在手里看，品质还行，但颜色不够深，跟她在广州见过的最好那批差了一个档次。她把箱子重新封好，在上面写了“二等品”三个字。
桂姨推门进来，手里端着一碗绿豆汤。这已经是她今天第三次送绿豆汤了，沈南枝每次都说“放那儿”，喝不喝看心情。
“南枝，外面有人找你。”
“不认识。一个女的，穿得挺体面，说是从港城来的。”
沈南枝手里的紫水晶差点掉了。
港城。
她把石头放回箱子里，拍了拍手上的灰，站起来。走到门口的时候，她停了一下，把工作服的袖子放下来，扣好扣子，又把头发拢了拢。
店门口站着一个人。三十来岁的女人，穿着一件深灰色的西装外套，里面是白色的真丝衬衫，下面是一条黑色的直筒裙，脚上穿着黑色的低跟皮鞋。头发盘在脑后，用一根簪子别着，脸上化了淡妆，嘴唇涂了一层薄薄的口红，颜色不艳。
她站在那里，腰板挺得笔直，手里拎着一个黑色的公文包，姿态很端正，像在等人。
看见沈南枝出来，她微微点了下头。
“请问是沈南枝沈老板吗？”
“是我。”
“我姓何，何婉清。港城周氏珠宝，周总让我来的。”
沈南枝愣了一下。周志豪派来的人？怎么不提前打个招呼？
何婉清像是看穿了她的疑惑，从公文包里拿出一个信封，递过来。信封上印着周氏珠宝的logo，封口处盖了周志豪的私章。
沈南枝拆开，里面是一封信，周志豪亲笔写的，字迹潦草但能辨认——“南枝，这是我的侄女婉清，在港城做了八年珠宝销售。让她去你那边帮你一阵子，展会的筹备她熟。周志豪。”
沈南枝把信看了两遍，抬头看何婉清。
何婉清站在那里，表情没什么变化，不笑也不板着脸，就是很平静地等着。沈南枝注意到她的站姿很专业，重心在两只脚上均匀分布，不靠门框不靠墙，手自然垂在身侧。
“何小姐，请进。”
何婉清进了店，目光扫了一圈，不紧不慢的，跟陈志远那种“扫视”不一样，她看得很细，但不是盯着看，是扫过去就记住了。走到柜台前，她停下来，看了一眼那盆茉莉花，又看了一眼旁边玻璃瓶里的野花，目光在那两盆花上停了一秒。
“这个位置放展示台，”她指了指柜台旁边靠墙的地方，“一米二高，玻璃罩，里面打暖光。银花系列放在这里，顾客一进门就能看见。”
沈南枝没说话。
“周总说你在准备港城珠宝展，”何婉清转过身，看着她，“我帮你把产品线捋一遍，该补的补，该砍的砍。展位设计、产品陈列、宣传册、价格体系，这些我都做过。时间还剩四个月，够用了。”
她说这些话的时候语气很平，像在念菜单。不是征求沈南枝的意见，是在告诉她“我要做什么”。
沈南枝看了她两秒钟。
content_en:
After Chen Zhiyuan's call, Shen Nanzhi was busy for a whole week.
The order for the Yinhua series has not come yet, but she has to prepare all the materials first. The 0.3mm silver wire was not available in Jinghai, so she asked Chen Zhiyuan to send fifty rolls from Binhai. The shipping cost was more expensive than the silver wire itself. The stock of amethyst and rose quartz was not enough, so she contacted the supplier in Guangzhou and ordered a batch urgently, but the other party said she would have to wait ten days.
You can't be idle these ten days. She asked all six female workers in the county to make basic beaded jewelry. The ten people in Jinghai were divided into two groups. One group did the regular replenishment of "Jinghai Spring", and the other group learned the silver weaving technique from her.
The process of teaching people was much more tiring than she thought.
Among the ten people, Sister-in-law Zhang is the most dexterous. Although she is tall and thick, her fingers are as thick as carrots, but she can hold the silver thread very steadily, her hands do not shake when she makes the first circle, and the thread ends are hidden cleanly when she finishes. Shen Nanzhi taught her three times and she learned it. Although the speed was slow and it took more than 20 minutes to weave a flower, at least the weaved thing was readable.
There were two young girls who were good with their hands and learned quickly, but they were impatient. After braiding two flowers, they felt it was enough and started chatting and joking. Shen Nanzhi placed the flowers they had knitted side by side on the table, pointed to one of the flowers with crooked petals and said, "If you sell this, no one will take 30 cents." The two girls blushed, lowered their heads and continued practicing.
The remaining seven cannot be taught no matter how you teach them. Either their hands were shaking or they were going in the wrong direction, and some couldn't even hold the pliers steady. Shen Nanzhi did not force them and asked them to go back and continue making beads, and the piece rate would remain the same.
In the end, only Mrs. Zhang and the two young girls were able to make silver flowers by hand. Four people, including Shen Nanzhi himself, can weave up to forty or fifty silver flowers every day, which is far from enough.
She needs more people, better people.
This problem has been running around in my mind for several days, but I haven't found a solution.
That evening, Shen Nanzhi was counting materials in the warehouse. The silver thread has reached thirty rolls, and there are still twenty rolls on the way. Two boxes of amethyst came. She opened one box, grabbed a handful and looked at it in her hand. The quality was okay, but the color was not dark enough, and it was not as good as the best batch she had seen in Guangzhou. She resealed the box and wrote the words "Second Class" on it.
Aunt Gui opened the door and came in, holding a bowl of mung bean soup in her hand. This is the third time she has given mung bean soup today. Shen Nanzhi always says "put it there" and whether to drink it or not depends on her mood.
"Nanzhi, someone is looking for you outside."
"Who?"
"I don't know her. A woman, well-dressed, said she came from Hong Kong City."
Shen Nanzhi almost dropped the amethyst in his hand.
Port city.
She put the stone back into the box, dusted her hands, and stood up. When she reached the door, she paused, put down the sleeves of her overalls, buttoned them up, and pushed her hair back.
There was a man standing at the door of the store. The woman in her thirties was wearing a dark gray suit jacket, a white silk shirt underneath, a black straight skirt, and black low-heeled leather shoes. Her hair was tied back and pinned with a hairpin. She wore light makeup on her face and a thin layer of lipstick on her lips, which was not bright in color.
She stood there with her back straight and a black briefcase in her hand. Her posture was very upright, as if she was waiting for someone.
Seeing Shen Nanzhi coming out, she nodded slightly.
"Is this Boss Shen Nanzhi Shen?"
"It's me."
"My surname is He, He Wanqing. Mr. Zhou asked me to come to Hong Kong City Zhou's Jewelry."
Shen Nanzhi was stunned for a moment. Someone sent by Zhou Zhihao? Why don't you say hello in advance?
He Wanqing seemed to see through her doubts, took out an envelope from her briefcase and handed it over. The envelope was printed with the logo of Zhou's Jewelry, and the seal was stamped with Zhou Zhihao's personal seal.
Shen Nanzhi opened it and found a letter inside, written by Zhou Zhihao himself. The handwriting was sloppy but legible - "Nanzhi, this is my niece Wanqing, who has been selling jewelry in Hong Kong City for eight years. Ask her to help you for a while. She is familiar with the preparation of the exhibition. Zhou Zhihao."
Shen Nanzhi read the letter twice and looked up at He Wanqing.
He Wanqing stood there, her expression unchanged, neither smiling nor keeping a straight face, just waiting calmly. Shen Nanzhi noticed that her standing posture was very professional, with her center of gravity evenly distributed on her two feet, neither leaning against the door frame nor the wall, and her hands hanging naturally by her sides.
"Miss He, please come in."
He Wanqing entered the store and glanced around, unhurriedly. It was different from Chen Zhiyuan's "scanning". She looked very carefully, but she didn't stare at it, she just scanned it and remembered it. When she reached the counter, she stopped, glanced at the pot of jasmine flowers, and then at the wild flowers in the glass vase next to her. Her eyes paused on the two pots of flowers for a second.
"This is where the display stand is placed," she pointed to the wall next to the counter. "It's one meter high, with a glass cover and warm light inside. The Silver Flower series is placed here, and customers can see it as soon as they enter."
Shen Nanzhi said nothing.
"President Zhou said that you are preparing for the Hong Kong City Jewelry Exhibition," He Wanqing turned around and looked at her, "I will help you go through the product line, add what should be added, and cut off what should be cut. I have done all these things including booth design, product display, brochures, and price systems. There are still four months left, which is enough."
She said these words in a calm tone, as if she was reading from a menu. He was not asking for Shen Nanzhi's opinion, but telling her "what I want to do."
Shen Nanzhi looked at her for two seconds.
